VERSION.value: github.com/ka9q/libfec master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: libfec (1995-, Phil Karn KA9Q): optimised VITERBI decoders for convolutional codes (the trellis / add-compare-select / traceback machinery) plus Reed-Solomon; the amateur-radio and deep-space FEC reference

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: maximum-likelihood decoding of noisy coded signals (hidden-state estimation)

value.built_to: recover the most-likely transmitted bit sequence from a noisy convolutionally-coded signal by the Viterbi algorithm (dynamic programming over a trellis of hidden encoder states), and to correct Reed-Solomon block errors
value.pressure: channel noise on band-limited links (satellite, deep space, radio); the decoder must find the maximum-likelihood path through an exponential state space in linear time
value.success_means: decoded bit-error rate at or below the code's theoretical curve for a given SNR; the self-tests pass

ANCESTRY.value: libfec (1995-, Phil Karn KA9Q): optimised VITERBI decoders for convolutional codes (the trellis / add-compare-select / traceback machinery) plus Reed-Solomon; the amateur-radio and deep-space FEC reference

environment.obstruction_2026-09-12: libfec's Viterbi decoders ship hand-written 32-bit x86 MMX/SSE assembly (mmxbfly27.s: `push` with 32-bit suffixes) that will not assemble on x86-64, and its 1990s configure emits an invalid -march=x86_64. The portable C path (viterbi27_port.c) exists but the lib target forces the SIMD objects. A faithful run needs an i386 world (gcc -m32 / a 32-bit container) = RUNNABLE_HISTORICAL_TOOLCHAIN, queued. Source is pinned+hashed; nothing modernised. This is a preserved 'needs an old machine' fossil, not a failure.

cut.note: three decoders for two code families plus DSP helpers; the SIMD files are the same machinery re-expressed for four instruction sets (a preservation of the 2004 hardware pressure, not new anatomy)

organs.human_interpretation: maximum-likelihood decoding of a convolutional code by dynamic programming over the encoder's 64 states
organs.mechanism: create (branch tables) -> init (metrics = 63, start state 0) -> update_blk (one butterfly sweep per data bit, decisions stored) -> chainback (walk the decisions from the end state) ; the same four calls exist for K=9 (viterbi29), K=15 (viterbi615) and K=24 (viterbi224)
organs.state: two 64-entry metric buffers + one decision word per bit

organs.mechanism: for each of 32 butterfly indices, Branchtab[k][state] = 255 if parity(2*state & POLY_k) else 0: the symbol the encoder WOULD emit leaving that state; at decode time (table XOR received soft symbol) is the branch distance, so the two branches of a butterfly have complementary costs metric and 510-metric
assumptions: both polynomials odd (fano.c 88-90 states the same assumption) so the pair of branches is complementary

organs.mechanism: for butterfly i (states i and i+32 -> states 2i and 2i+1): m0 = old[i] + metric, m1 = old[i+32] + (510 - metric); keep the smaller into new[2i] and record the choice as one decision bit; repeat with the metrics swapped for new[2i+1]; after 32 butterflies swap the old/new buffer pointers; metrics are never renormalised (unsigned wrap is tolerated by the signed comparison)
assumptions: 64 states fit; the best path's metric difference stays below 2^31
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the whole decoding cost is here; every SIMD file re-expresses this macro

organs.mechanism: starting from endstate (<<2 to align with the decision bit layout) and past the 6 tail bits, for each bit from the last: read the decision bit of the current state, shift it in as the new high bit of the state and of the output byte; the register value IS the decoded byte every 8 steps
assumptions: the encoder was flushed to a known end state (tail)

organs.human_name: Reed-Solomon codec (parametrised: symsize, gfpoly, fcr, prim, nroots, pad)
organs.mechanism: init builds the field and generator; encode divides by the generator; decode = syndromes -> (erasure seed) -> Berlekamp-Massey -> Chien -> Forney; the same header is #included three times for char / int / CCSDS symbol types
organs.state: the field tables and generator (per code)
organs.source_boundary: the three *_rs.h templates and their instantiations

organs.mechanism: run a shift register from 1: alpha_to[i] = sr, index_of[sr] = i, sr <<= 1, reduce by gfpoly on overflow; after nn steps sr must return to 1 or the polynomial is not primitive (refused); then build genpoly = prod (x - alpha^(fcr + i*prim)) by repeated multiplication in index form
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: all field multiplication in the codec is a table add mod nn

organs.mechanism: for each data symbol: feedback = log(data ^ parity[0]); shift the parity register by one; parity[j] ^= alpha^(feedback + genpoly[nroots-j]); the remainder after all data symbols is the parity
s[i] = received(alpha^(fcr+i)) for i < nroots by Horner's rule over the block; if all zero the block is a codeword and decoding stops (count 0)

lambda starts as the erasure locator (product over known erasure positions, 92-100); then for r from no_eras+1 to nroots: discrepancy = sum lambda[i] * s[r-i-1]; if zero shift b; else lambda = lambda - discr*x*b with b updated from the old lambda when 2*el <= r+no_eras-1 (the length test); deg(lambda) is the number of errors+erasures found
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: a locator of degree != number of roots later found is reported as uncorrectable (count = -1, line 239-244)

organs.mechanism: evaluate lambda at every field element by keeping one running register per coefficient (reg[j] += j each step) and XORing; each zero gives a root and its location number; refuse if the root count != deg_lambda
omega = s * lambda mod x^nroots; for each root X: num1 = omega(1/X), num2 = X^(fcr-1) factor, den = lambda'(1/X) (the odd-power terms); error = num1*num2/den XORed into data at loc

organs.human_interpretation: decode the same convolutional code as Viterbi but by exploring one path at a time, going deeper while the accumulated metric stays above a threshold and backing up when it drops
organs.mechanism: precompute per-node branch metrics from a metric table; at each node try the better branch first (sorted tm[0], tm[1]); move forward if gamma + branch >= t, tightening t by multiples of delta on first visits; otherwise back up and try the other branch, loosening t by delta when both are exhausted; stop at the last node or after maxcycles*nbits cycles (a decoding FAILURE with the cycle count returned)
organs.output: decoded bits, final metric, cycles used
organs.state: an array of nodes (metrics[4], tm[2], gamma, encstate, i), threshold t
assumptions: a good frame needs few cycles; effort grows with noise (the sequential-decoding computation distribution)
tail is zero so the last K-1 nodes have one branch
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: long constraint lengths (K=32 here) where Viterbi's 2^(K-1) states are impossible; pays with variable and unbounded effort
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: timeout (returns 0 with cycles = maxcycles) is the designed failure

organs.mechanism: for each of 256 received bins compute P(bin | 0 sent) and P(bin | 1 sent) as differences of the normal CDF at bin edges shifted by +/- signal and scaled by 1/noise; metric = log2(p/(p0+p1)/2) - bias, scaled and rounded; bias = 0 for Viterbi, the code rate for sequential decoding (the Fano metric)
assumptions: AWGN; 8-bit quantised soft decisions with bins centred on integers
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: makes the decoders soft-decision; the bias term is what makes Fano's threshold test meaningful

organs.mechanism: sum a[i] * coeffs[i] over len in 16-bit fixed point; the SIMD variants keep several shifted copies of the coefficients to align loads (the portable one keeps one)

pressures.source_evidence: the whole library; metrics.c models the channel
pressures.condition: a channel flips or perturbs each transmitted symbol independently with some probability; the receiver sees only the corrupted sequence and knows the code; redundancy costs bandwidth so it is fixed in advance
pressures.failure_condition: bit/frame error rate above what the application tolerates at the operating SNR
pressures.world_punishes: decoding that ignores soft information or the code's structure
pressures.world_rewards: exploiting structure (trellis or algebra) to reach the code's correction capacity
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: majority vote on repetition (works, far from capacity); a world must charge for redundancy
pressures.cheat_control: a decoder given the transmitted bits must show BER 0; a world that scores it equal to a real decoder at high noise is not measuring correction
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: deliver bits over a noisy link (satellite, amateur radio)

pressures.condition: frames are usually clean and occasionally very noisy; a decoder with fixed cost pays the worst case always, one with variable cost pays for the noise it meets but may not finish
pressures.failure_condition: timeout on a noisy frame (Fano) versus a state count that cannot be afforded at all (Viterbi at K=32)
pressures.world_punishes: fixed cost when noise is rare; unbounded cost when noise is common
pressures.world_rewards: an early-exit search whose failure is detectable and cheap to fall back from
pressures.observable_consequence: the distribution of cycles per frame; timeout rate vs SNR
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: always run the exhaustive decoder (only possible for short constraint lengths)
pressures.cheat_control: a search told the true path must use ~1 cycle per bit; if the world does not reward that, effort is not being measured
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: same, at long constraint length

pressures.source_evidence: record: RS decoder present beside Viterbi; CCSDS concatenation files
pressures.condition: corruption hits runs of bits (fading, a scratched medium), so a bit-level code sees many errors in one place while a symbol-level code sees few corrupted symbols
pressures.failure_condition: bit-level decoders fail on bursts they could survive if spread
pressures.world_punishes: treating burst errors as independent bit errors
pressures.world_rewards: grouping bits into symbols (RS) or spreading errors (an interleaver -- NOT in this body)
pressures.observable_consequence: frame error rate under burst vs random noise at equal bit-error rate
pressures.cheat_control: a decoder told the burst boundaries must correct up to nroots/2 symbol errors regardless of bit count
